The statement stays true without it. If some s ∈ f.support has s ≠ r, the existing proof goes through unchanged; it uses the hypothesis only to obtain such an s. Otherwise every s ∈ f.support equals r (an empty support is a special case). By the definition at line 175, planeExponentDifference r r = fun i => (r i : ℤ) - (r i : ℤ) = 0. Take v := fun _ => 1, which is nonzero, and k := 0 for each s; then 0 • v = 0 = planeExponentDifference r s. A by_cases on `∃ s ∈ f.support, s ≠ r` therefore gives a proof without the hypothesis.
